text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Another bloody provocation as two Greek Cypriot soldiers kill one Turkish Cypriot soldier and injure another guarding the border on the divided island.
- Coalition economy officials are looking for a compromise formula before heading to the U.S. for an International Monetary Fund meeting.
- Fresh troubles for the coalition as economy officials meet without inviting ministers from the Islamist wing of the government.
- Bureaucrats are concerned by Deputy Prime Minister Ciller's consideration of the Mexico model as a possible way of securing international financial support for Turkey.
- Turkey's Industrialists and Businessmen's Association warns of an economic crisis, exacerbated by the government's policies.

- Iraqi Kurd faction leader Talabani says Turkish Prime Minister Erbakan reached an agreement with Iraqi President Saddam Hussein on helping rival Kurd leader Barzani to establish an autonomous region in northern Iraq.
- Despite pessimistic expectations for the economy, investments in July were at a high level.
- Turkey's defence industry is looking increasingly to supply the country's defence needs.
